extracted.intended_audience: development staff and grant writers at Catholic nonprofit organizations (nonprofit grantseekers)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance on common mistakes to avoid when preparing grant proposals for foundations and funders, tailored to Catholic nonprofit organizations. Focuses on proposal presentation, alignment with funder priorities, measurable outcomes, budgeting, timelines, and stakeholder readiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to Proofread
rubrics_metrics.description: Using proper grammar, spelling, punctuation, and formatting demonstrates professionalism and attention to detail; proposals must be read thoroughly before submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have a team member proofread; if solo, recruit a colleague or read the proposal out loud to catch errors and areas needing clarification. Proofreading also identifies unclear passages that could undermine reviewer confidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing with Your Organization in Mind
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing primarily to showcase your organization rather than addressing the grant maker's interests undermines the proposal's effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Know your audience and demonstrate understanding of the funder's motivations and philanthropic interests. Emphasize how the requested funds will advance the funder's mission and desired impact, not just how they help your organization. Tailor each proposal specifically to the funder; avoid careless copy-paste and re-read pasted sections for alignment with the foundation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of Specific Metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to provide tangible, trackable metrics leaves funders unsure how you will measure success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify clear, quantifiable indicators that will be used to evaluate the project so funders can judge impact and accountability. Tie metrics to outcomes funders value to boost confidence in your ability to deliver results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiting Until the Last Minute
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitting proposals at the last minute risks technical problems, rushed content, and missed deadlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan ahead with a fundraising calendar and set internal completion goals several weeks before the due date. Submit early when possible to avoid website malfunctions, fax or mail delays, and to allow time for revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: No Clear Buy-in from Key Staff and Stakeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: Applying for grants without organizational capacity and stakeholder commitment can lead to failure to implement the project and damage funder relationships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure leadership and relevant departments understand and support the project; involve staff, volunteers, and stakeholders to clarify roles, responsibilities, potential roadblocks, and mitigation strategies. Confirm the organization can realistically complete the proposed work to build trust with funders and enable long-term relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using Jargon
rubrics_metrics.description: Relying on technical language unfamiliar to funders can obscure your proposal's meaning and weaken its persuasiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid jargon; explain terms in plain language unless the funder is a specialist in your field. Get to know the funder to determine the appropriate level of technical vocabulary that will resonate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ignoring Foundation Requests or Preferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Not following a funder's specified proposal length, content, or format requirements can result in rejection or a negative impression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully read and conform to foundation instructions. When repurposing content from other proposals, adapt it to meet the specific foundation's requests and formatting rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leaving the Grant Maker Wondering, 'So What?'
rubrics_metrics.description: Describing activities and outputs without connecting them to broader outcomes or the human impact fails to convey true significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complement quantifiable metrics with narrative or examples that put a 'face' to the project and explain deeper impacts (e.g., how meals improve concentration and academic outcomes). Make clear why the work matters beyond raw numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unexplained Budget
rubrics_metrics.description: Presenting a budget without clear justification or accurate cost estimates undermines credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be meticulous: obtain quotes or research to support figures, choose a clear budget format if one isn't provided, and be ready to justify anticipated expenses if asked. Ensure budget line items clearly explain how and where funds will be spent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overpromising
rubrics_metrics.description: Setting unrealistic project goals, timelines, or expected outcomes raises the risk of failure and harms funder relationships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep objectives achievable and timelines realistic; anticipate parts of the project that may take longer than expected. Avoid promising outcomes you cannot reliably deliver—funders are more forgiving of unanticipated delays than of unmet commitments.
